headline: Pelicans fans are weary of waiting on Zion, not angry
summary: New Orleans is a Saints, LSU and Mardi Gras town first. The Pelicans hold a loyal, modest slice of it, strongest among diehards who stayed through the Hornets-to-Pelicans change. Two straight sub-30-win seasons (26-56 last year) have left the mood weary, not angry. Fans wear the city alongside the team: fleur-de-lis, purple-green-gold, local brands next to navy and gold. The best City Editions did the same.

insights.title: Saints first, Pels second
insights.detail: Football, LSU and Carnival dominate the calendar and the closet. Pelicans gear competes with black-and-gold Saints and purple-and-gold LSU apparel for the same wardrobe slot. Pelicans passion is real but concentrated, and it peaks when the team tells a New Orleans story instead of a generic NBA one.
insights.implication: Lead Pelicans product with city iconography (fleur-de-lis, Carnival, second line), not team marks alone. Don't copy Saints black and gold.

insights.title: Fatigue, not fury
insights.detail: Last season ended 26-56, the second straight sub-30-win year, with no playoffs. Now fans face a coach change from Willie Green to Jamahl Mosley, no 2026 first-round pick (traded to Atlanta in the Derik Queen deal) and a quiet summer.
insights.implication: Keep early-season product and campaigns about the city and the young core, not championship promises. Trey Murphy III, Queen and Fears are safer faces than anything built on Zion's availability.

insights.title: Zion is the brand, Murphy is the trust
insights.detail: Zion Williamson draws national attention and the biggest jersey and sneaker interest. Years of injuries have made fans wary of hanging their identity on him. Trey Murphy III averaged 21.5 ppg and survived June trade rumors. Locals admire him as a homegrown-feeling scorer.
insights.implication: Balance Zion signature product with Murphy and young-core pieces, so one availability story doesn't govern the line. Zion is already a Jordan Brand athlete, so coordinate any Jordan crossover.

insights.title: Hornets memory runs deep
insights.detail: Older fans remember the 2002-2013 Hornets: Chris Paul, David West, Tyson Chandler, Byron Scott. They remember the 2005-07 Oklahoma City exile after Katrina too. Teal and purple Hornets throwbacks still circulate, and the Pelicans name only arrived in 2013.
insights.implication: A teal and purple heritage nod could land with these fans. The Hornets name and marks belong to Charlotte, so clear the licensing first.

insights.title: City Edition is the fan favorite
insights.detail: Per the current facts, the 2025-26 City Edition revived the fan-favorite 2023-24 design. That signals fans reward local stories and punish the generic. The 2023-24 "NOLA Nights" edition (purple and neon green, a skeletal "Skelican") shows they prefer a nocturnal, local look to plain team color.
insights.implication: Make the City Edition the market's anchor drop. Pair it with a lifestyle capsule built on Carnival color blocking, made with local collaborators.

insights.title: Don't lift Black Masking Indian imagery
insights.detail: Black Masking Indian suits are sacred community traditions, and the maskers spend a full year making them. The same goes for the Tremé and Seventh Ward second-line brass-band culture. Fans love and display the culture, but the community guards it.
insights.implication: Credit and pay Black New Orleans partners for any reference. Never reproduce the suits as a pattern. Safer cues are the bold, unaffiliated looks of Carnival parades, social aid and pleasure club umbrella and sash colors, and brass-band typography.

places.name: Smoothie King Center
places.why: The Pelicans' home sits next to the Caesars Superdome, and gameday crowds share the footprint with Saints football.

places.name: Caesars Superdome
places.why: The Saints' home is the town's biggest sports cathedral. It sets the black-and-gold gameday template Pelicans fans live beside.

places.name: Mother's Restaurant
places.why: A long-standing local institution near the arena, known for ferdi special po-boys and ham.

places.name: Frenchmen Street
places.why: The live-music corridor where locals gather before and after games, with brass bands and jazz as the soundtrack.

places.name: Congo Square (Armstrong Park)
places.why: The historic gathering place for African and Afro-Creole music and dance, and the anchor for any respectful community work.

places.name: Bayou St. John
places.why: A casual Sunday hangout for locals and a good lifestyle backdrop.

places.name: Tulane University and Loyola area uptown courts
places.why: College basketball and rec courts that tie the local hooper community to the city.

people.name: Zion Williamson
people.why: The franchise's most famous player and biggest jersey and shoe draw, with a complicated, hopeful fan relationship.

people.name: Trey Murphy III
people.why: The breakout scorer who averaged 21.5 ppg. June trade rumors made fans fiercely protective of him.

people.name: Derik Queen
people.why: A young big man acquired in the trade that cost the 2026 first-round pick, and now central to the rebuilding hope.

people.name: Jeremiah Fears
people.why: A young guard fans see as a future creator for the team.

people.name: Jamahl Mosley
people.why: First-year coach, hired from Orlando in May after Willie Green was dismissed.

people.name: Anthony Davis
people.why: The unibrow-era face of the Pelicans brand, and in fan memory the franchise's defining homegrown star.

people.name: Chris Paul
people.why: The Hornets-era superstar whose New Orleans years older fans remember most fondly.

people.name: Pete Maravich
people.role: LSU and New Orleans Jazz legend
people.why: Pistol Pete is the Louisiana basketball myth, and his floppy-socks era feeds the state's hoops identity.

moments.name: Season opener and NBA Cup run
moments.why: The Pelicans are in West Group B with OKC, MIN, LAC and MEM. Cup play opens Oct 30 at the Clippers, the first chance to sell local hope.

moments.name: Saints football season overlap
moments.why: Football competes for fans' attention and wardrobe all fall and winter. Schedule basketball around Saints Sundays, not against them.

moments.name: Christmas and Reveillon season
moments.why: Family gifting peaks, and the Pelicans aren't on the national Christmas Day slate, so local holiday merchandising matters.

moments.name: Carnival season and Mardi Gras
moments.timing: Twelfth Night (Jan 6) through Fat Tuesday, which falls in February 2027
moments.why: The biggest color and culture moment of the year, when purple, green and gold override team colors across the city.

moments.name: New Orleans Jazz and Heritage Festival
moments.why: A peak for local pride and fashion, overlapping with the end of the NBA regular season.

moments.name: NBA draft and free agency
moments.why: Hope and anxiety for a fan base that has watched picks traded and stars leave.

vocabulary.meaning: Fans' and media's shorthand for the Pelicans.
Louisiana's playful spelling of go, as in Geaux Tigers. It turns up in chants and gear across the state.
The Saints' signature chant. It marks the football-first culture and isn't a Pelicans phrase.
The brass-band parade tradition, with followers dancing behind the main line. Shorthand for communal celebration.
Local word for a street median, and a quick insider tell.
Classic New Orleans greeting, and the name of the local accent group.
The crowd's Carnival call to riders on the floats.
The French heraldic lily, the city's best-known emblem. It appears on Saints and Pelicans-adjacent gear alike.

designCues.cue: Pelicans navy as the base field
designCues.use: Anchor Association and lifestyle product with it, so team identity stays legible.

designCues.cue: Old-gold accent distinct from Saints metallic
designCues.source: A brass-like accent chosen for this brief; the official Pelicans gold is #85714D
designCues.use: Use as a brass-like accent that reads New Orleans, not Saints.

designCues.source: Mardi Gras royal purple, representing justice
designCues.use: Use for color blocking in Carnival capsule drops, tied to the season from Twelfth Night through Fat Tuesday.
Use as a secondary pop on warm-up and lifestyle pieces during Carnival.
Use as a tonal embossed or woven accent, redrawn in distinct proportions so it doesn't mimic the Saints mark.
Use as a fine tonal jacquard on trims, hems and lining, stylized rather than literal.

designCues.cue: Shotgun house and bright-paint color story
designCues.source: Neighborhood architecture of the Seventh Ward, Marigny and Bywater
designCues.use: Use as a color-block palette for a rotating lifestyle capsule, credited to local architectural heritage.

designCues.source: Hand-painted show posters and social aid and pleasure club banners
designCues.use: Use on graphic tees and hoodies, and commission a local lettering artist.

productHooks: Carnival-season capsule in purple, green and Pelicans navy and gold, launching in January and ending Fat Tuesday, made with a New Orleans lettering artist or collective.
Tonal fleur-de-lis and iron-lace jacquard warm-up and shooting shirt, tied to the City Edition story.
Player-led tees and kids' jerseys for Murphy, Queen and Fears, so the line doesn't depend on Zion.
Hornets-era heritage nod in teal and purple, only if licensing with the NBA and Charlotte is cleared.
Family-sized and youth Icon and Statement jerseys as a lower-priced way in, since the base is local and family-heavy.
watchouts: Mardi Gras Indian suits, chants and Black Masking Indian imagery are sacred community traditions. Never reproduce them as a pattern. If you reference them at all, partner with credited, paid community members.
The fleur-de-lis is tied to the Saints, so a derivative mark risks looking like NFL product and may raise third-party licensing issues.
Charlotte and the NBA control the Hornets name, teal and Hugo imagery. Any heritage use needs clearance.
Zion's availability history can make hero-driven campaigns brittle. Don't depend on a single athlete.
Avoid caricature in New Orleans iconography, such as jazz-hands, voodoo and excess Bourbon Street tropes.

segments.reach: Pelicans local radio and social, local watch spots and the Smoothie King Center.

segments.description: Suburban and West Bank families who come for the experience and the promotions.

extra.sentiment: Weary and cautious. After a 26-56 season, a coaching change to Jamahl Mosley, no 2026 first-round pick and a quiet offseason under Joe Dumars, fans are lowering expectations. They protect Trey Murphy III, hope for Derik Queen and Jeremiah Fears, and still wait on Zion Williamson.
extra.gamedayLook: Navy and gold Pelicans jerseys (Zion, Murphy, throwback Davis), Hornets-era teal or purple throwbacks on older fans, and Saints and LSU gear mixed in. Everything else is summer-weight New Orleans casual: breathable tees, caps and sneakers made for the heat.
